How to use an online tasbeeh counter

Reading time: 3 minutes · 14 October 2026

It is not always easy to keep count while doing tasbeeh. A digital tasbeeh counter on your phone makes it simple: you just keep tapping and the count rises by itself.

How to use it

  1. Choose a target: 33, 99, 100 or free.
  2. Tap the big button each time you say the dhikr shown.
  3. When the target is reached the tool tells you and moves to the next dhikr by itself.
  4. Press “Reset” to take the count back to zero.

Choosing a target

  • 33 / 99 / 100: each dhikr that many times, then the next one appears.
  • Free: no limit; keep going as long as you like.

The after-prayer tasbeeh

A hadith mentions saying SubhanAllah 33 times, Alhamdulillah 33 times and Allahu Akbar 34 times after prayer (Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim). Reports can differ slightly in detail, so check the full order in a reliable book or with a scholar. In the tool, choose a target of 33, then switch to “Free” for the third dhikr to count up to 34.

Masnoon duas and wazaif

The same page has masnoon duas (for waking, eating, travelling and more) and a few well-known wazaif, with meaning and source. To confirm the Arabic text, check a reliable book such as Hisn al-Muslim.

Today's total and the screen

The tool shows today's total count, and the “Keep screen awake” button (where your phone allows it) stops the screen turning off while you count. Your count is saved only in your phone's browser.
